html:
The Tuareg are the Berber nomads of the central and western Sahara. Here, labelled "Touareg" in 1279, they cover a huge stretch of desert from the Atlantic side to the Aïr mountains. See also the earlier map label, Tuaregs.

In the 13th century the Sahara's trade was booming. The Mali Empire had risen to the south, and caravans carried its gold north and brought back salt, cloth and copper. The Tuareg controlled wells and passes on these routes, and earned their living by guiding, protecting, taxing and sometimes raiding the caravans of the trans-Saharan trade.

The Tuareg town of Takedda mined and traded copper; Ibn Battuta passed through it in 1353. Tuareg groups also lived around Timbuktu, which they took from Mali in 1433. In the 15th century the sultanate of Agadez grew up in the Aïr.
